newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Stocks ignored, crude dominates.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Stocks ignored, crude dominates.

text.p: The overnight weakness of Brent crude kept the high sulphur fuel oil market quiet on Friday with prices quoted slightly softer than in previous sessions, traders said.
Sentiment was sluggish and most traders were sidelined, with one bid for the 180-cst grade heard at $98.50 a tonne.
"As crude has been weak in the past few days and it seems the local trader (who has been supporting the market) does not take any action, most people just stay away from the market," said one trader.
On Thursday, the 180-cst grade was offered at $99.50 per tonne against an earlier $100.50 for late April delivery, compared with Wednesday's $100.50 traded level.
The market was indifferent after the Trade Development Board (TDB) announced on Thursday the lowest level of Singapore residual fuel oil stocks in at least three years, traders said.
The TDB data showed a drop of 2.435 million barrels to 8.229 million barrels in the week ending April 2.
"The TDB data is supposed to support prices but the crude movements are far more influential," said one trader.
Chinese enquiries did not emerge this week, after two were heard late last week, which also added pressure to prices, traders said.
